sections.skill: Decide from results whether to continue, change or stop

questions.prompt: Target: 20 paid bookings in a month. Result: 26 bookings. What is the sensible decision?

choices.text: Continue
Stop
Ignore the result
Change the target to 40 and call it a failure

questions.correct_answer: Continue
questions.intro: After a test, decide: continue, change, or stop. CONTINUE when the results meet the target you set in advance. CHANGE (sometimes called a pivot) when part of the idea works but something important does not: a different customer, price, or offer might fit better. STOP when the results are far below the target and nothing points to a better version, or when the cost of continuing is too high. Stopping is not failing; it protects time and money for a better idea.
questions.feedback: Results above the target support continuing.

questions.prompt: Target: 20 bookings. Result: 3 bookings, and customers said the price was fine but the hours did not suit them. What fits best?

questions.prompt: Most cookies sold. What is the choice?

choices.text: Ignore
Continue
Change
Stop

questions.correct_answer: Continue
questions.intro: Think of baking a new cookie for a school sale. If most cookies sell, keep making them (continue). If people love the taste but say the cookies are too big for the price, make them smaller (change). If almost no one buys and no one says why, try a different treat (stop). The decision follows the results and what people told you, not how much you hoped it would work.
questions.feedback: Good results mean continue.

sections.skill: Apply it: decide with stated targets and feedback

Stop, because tutoring never works
